sentences.text:
Applicant :- Narsingh Prajapati Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Ajay Kumar,Arun Kumar,Harendra Yadav Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Mukul Kumar Mishra Hon'ble Saurabh Srivastava,J.

1. Heard Sri Ajay Kumar, learned counsel for applicant and Sri Mukul Kumar Mishra, learned counsel for informant and learned AGA for State.
2.

By means of the instant bail application, applicant is seeking bail in Case Crime No. 325 of 2023,
under Section 498A, 323, 504, 377 IPC read with Section 3/4 of D.P. Act, Police Station- Atarauliya,
District- Azamgarh during pendency of trial.

3. It is the case of the applicant that under some misconception, lighter and heavy talks between husband and wife (applicant and informant) which is quite obvious and normal in day to day life,
culminated into lodging the FIR in shape of case crime no. 325 of 2023, under Section 498A, 323,
504, 377 of IPC read with Section 3/4 of D.P. Act and the applicant is languishing in jail since Narsingh Prajapati vs State Of U.P. on 12 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94957686/
1 16.11.2023.
4.

entities.text: Narsingh Prajapati vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the applicant informed that as and when applicant being the husband sent to jail, the mindset of the informant/wife has now been changed and she visited the jail for meeting her husband which shows that now there are ample chances for re-union between husband and wife and the same has been admitted by learned counsel for the informant on one condition that the bail application may be allowed but the clear statement has to be recorded by this Court that the applicant will lead normal life along with the informant being the married couple as husband and wife.
5. After hearing the arguments, and concern of their client by rival counsels appearing for the parties, it is the advice to the applicant to lead a normal life being the husband and wife, by way of forgetting the unfateful period spent during incarceration.

The instant matter is squarely covered with the chaupai written by Goswami Tulsidas in Ramcharitmanas which is quoted as under:
"'???? ?? ???? ?? ???? ?????, ?? ???? ?????? ? ??? ??????? '"

6. The above mentioned proverb is beyond doubt and once the married couple has decided to live a peaceful life, there should not be any judicial impediment in shape of critical loss and the complexities of the litigation pending between the parties.

7. On the above mentioned ground and considering the nature of offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, submissions of learned counsel for parties and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, this Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed with the intention and hope that both the parties in shape of husband and wife (applicant and informant) will lead a normal happy married life.

8. Let the applicant- Narsingh Prajapati involved in aforesaid case crime number be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to the following conditions:-
i. The applicant will not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
ii. The applicant will not pressurize/intimidate the prosecution witness.
iii. The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted and/ or the applicant shall make himself available for interrogation by a police officer as and when required.
iv. The applicant shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected, of the commission of which he is suspected.
v. The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him Narsingh Prajapati vs State Of U.P. on 12 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94957686/
2 from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
vi.

entities.text: Narsingh Prajapati vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The applicant shall not leave India without the previous permission of the Court.
vii. In the event, the applicant changes his residential address, the applicant shall inform the court concerned about new residential address in writing.
9. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution shall be at liberty to move bail cancellation application before this Court.

10. However, it is made clear that the observations made above may not be taken into consideration in any manner whatsoever by the learned Trial court while adjudicating or expediting the trial in the aforesaid case crime.

Order Date :- 12.3.2024 Shaswat  Narsingh Prajapati vs State Of U.P. on 12 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94957686/
